#2773. ‘Thank goodness he’s on our team’: Cooper Flagg makes history, Dallas Mavericks keep stacking wins

With the Dallas Mavericks down 13 points late in the first half on the second night of a back-to-back, Monday night at American Airlines Center looked very much like a schedule loss. Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving had other ideas, though, as they combined for 78 points, fueling Dallas past the Indiana Pacers in a wild finish, 125-122.

The win was the Mavericks' third straight and moved Dallas to 7-4 on the season. It also put the Mavs three games over .500 for the first time since March 1, 2025, a date that feels a lot longer ago than it actually is for anyone who has lived through the last two years of Mavericks basketball.

Think about where this franchise was not long ago. The Luka Doncic trade. Irving's torn ACL. A 26-56 season and back-to-back years without a playoff appearance. Oddsmakers set Dallas' win total at 34.5 before this season, and after an opening stretch that included Houston, San Antonio and Oklahoma City, a lot of people expected the Mavs to be scrapping just to stay afloat by mid-November.

Instead, the Mavs are stacking wins, Flagg looks like an MVP candidate in year two, and Irving looks like his old self before the ACL injury happened. Most importantly, the way the Mavs are winning these games feels sustainable. Here are some of the biggest storylines from Monday night's thriller.

DALLAS, TEXAS – NOVEMBER 9: Cooper Flagg #32 of the Dallas Mavericks dunks during the first half against the Indiana Pacers at American Airlines Center on November 9, 2026 in Dallas, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images) | Getty Images

Flagg was good in the first half, but he was on an entirely different level in the second.

The 19-year-old star scored 30 of his season-high 43 points after halftime, including 14 on 6-of-6 shooting in the third quarter and 16 more in the fourth. He finished 16-of-25 from the field, 3-of-6 from 3-point range and a perfect 8-of-8 at the free-throw line, adding 10 rebounds, six assists, three steals and a block for his fourth straight double-double.

Flagg became just the second teenager in NBA history to post at least 40 points, 10 rebounds and five assists in a game, joining Kevin Durant, who put up 42 points, 13 rebounds and six assists in the final game of his rookie season with Seattle in 2008. Per StatMuse, add the three steals, and Flagg is the first teenager ever with a 40-10-5-3 line.

It was also his fifth career 40-point game, as many as the next two teenagers on that list combined (LeBron James with three and Anthony Edwards with two). His 14th career 30-point game moved him into second place for the most by a player under 20, behind only James, and his seventh 35-point game tied James for the most by a teenager. And keep in mind, Flagg doesn't turn 20 until Dec. 21.

Mavericks head coach Dusty May pointed to how complete Flagg's scoring package has become.

"He gets to the rim," May said in his postgame media availability. "I think him almost being a left-handed player in the paint certainly helps. He's a great left-footed jumper, left-handed finisher. Then he's able to square in the air from 15, 17 feet. … The last couple of games, he's made some threes and he's making all of his free throws. That's how you put up the 43 points, where you do a little bit of everything."

It's almost unreal just how good Flagg already is, and May is just happy he's on his roster and not having to gameplan against him.

"He affects the game in so many ways and he makes the right plays as far as passing," May said. "Thank goodness he's on our team. It's unbelievable that he's a 19-year-old doing this."

Flagg's deadly midrange shot, which he worked on all offseason, is paying off in a big way, especially in clutch situations, where he leads the league in clutch points.

"I think just being able to get to my spots at a higher level and being more comfortable with that has allowed me to take a little bit of load off my body," Flagg said. "Just kind of stopping short, raising up over people. It's taxing going downhill all the way to the rim and trying to finish over seven-footers all night, every night. … Just trusting the work, trusting the spot work that I put in all summer long."

Through 11 games, the reigning Rookie of the Year is averaging 25.9 points, 6.9 rebounds, 6.9 assists and 2.2 steals per game. Again, given everything Mavs fans have been through over the last 21 months, this sort of euphoric rise back to genuine happiness watching these games is hard to believe.

DALLAS, TEXAS – NOVEMBER 9: Kyrie Irving #11 of the Dallas Mavericks celebrates after scoring a three point basket during the second half against the Indiana Pacers at American Airlines Center on November 9, 2026 in Dallas, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images) | Getty Images

Flagg was the closer on Monday night, but Irving was arguably the reason Dallas was still in the game in those closing moments.

Playing the second night of a back-to-back for the first time this season, a day after logging 28 minutes in a 130-93 win over Brooklyn, Irving poured in 35 points in a season-high 38 minutes. He knocked down a season-high seven 3-pointers on 10 attempts, went 3-of-3 at the line and finished a game-best plus-29.

After missing 19 months with the torn ACL he suffered in March 2025, Irving said he told his teammates in the locker room after Sunday's win that he planned to play.

"When you're in a combative sport such as basketball, some days are going to feel good, some days aren't, especially coming off an injury or a long period of time," Irving said. "So I just had to get my body back used to being in the flow of the game. … I was just feeling great, and just coming in to today."

May, who said plus-minus is often overblown in a one-game sample, made an exception for Irving in this one.

"His plus-29 tonight was very indicative of how important he is," May said. "When we were struggling to make shots in the first half, we thought we were generating really good looks. We just looked a little bit flat. I thought Kyrie's shot-making just kind of righted the ship for us."

It's still early, but seeing Irving look this healthy and proving to be a seamless fit next to Flagg bodes well for what this team can accomplish this year. Perhaps the last two years of the basketball injury gods punishing the Mavs will result in some good injury luck the rest of this season.

DALLAS, TEXAS – NOVEMBER 9: Cooper Flagg #32 of the Dallas Mavericks celebrates with teammate Kyrie Irving #11 of the Dallas Mavericks after scoring a basket during the second half against the Indiana Pacers at American Airlines Center on November 9, 2026 in Dallas, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images) | Getty Images

The most encouraging part of all of this is just how naturally Flagg and Irving shared the scoring load against Indiana. The two combined for 26 fourth-quarter points, including Dallas' first 13 of the period, and May said neither player blinks when the play call goes to the other.

"We're coming out of a timeout, we may draw up a play for one of them just because the other one might have an All-League defender on him, or whatever the case, and they never roll their eyes," May said. "They know when we're going to one of the two, the other one's very, very supportive because they have that much respect for each other."

Irving, an established champion who has shared the floor with more than a few superstars over his 15-year career, is grateful that he's able to be Flagg's teammate, despite the two players being on different ends of their careers.

"We keep calling him a teenager, but he plays way beyond his years. We've got to give him his flowers," Irving said. "Most young guys will probably move away from that contact, but it seems like this newer generation that's coming into our league, they fear nothing. And I think he falls right in line with that. So grateful to have him on the wing with me."

Those feelings are mutual for Flagg: "Just having [Kyrie] out there, his gravity opening the floor for everybody else, it makes my life so much easier."

DALLAS, TEXAS – NOVEMBER 9: P.J. Washington #25 of the Dallas Mavericks celebrates a three point basket during the second half against the Indiana Pacers at American Airlines Center on November 9, 2026 in Dallas, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images) | Getty Images

It wasn't pretty at the end, but it didn't have to be for the Mavs to come up with another win. That's one thing that's been so encouraging about this fast start to the season. Dallas is finding different ways to win, whether it's pretty or not.

Indiana's Pascal Siakam torched Dallas for 26 first-half points on 8-of-9 shooting, but the Mavs adjusted their help defense after the break and held him to just three points on 1-of-7 shooting the rest of the way. The Pacers took a 66-56 lead into halftime and a 93-90 lead into the fourth before Flagg buried a 26-foot pull-up 3 to tie it. Irving's 23-footer with 9:36 left put Dallas in front for good.

Leading 125-122 with a chance to put the game on ice, PJ Washington missed a pair of free throws with four seconds left, and Caleb Martin bailed everyone out by stealing Andrew Nembhard's inbounds pass to Siakam with 0.9 seconds remaining. Pacers head coach Rick Carlisle was adamant that Martin fouled Siakam on that final play, but judging from the replays, it looked like Martin got all ball before ever making any contact with Siakam.

It obviously would've been nice for Washington to sink at least one of those free throws to avoid that last-second drama, but again, the Mavs keep finding different ways to win. How many times over the past two years have we seen a game like that end in a loss for Dallas?

DALLAS, TEXAS – NOVEMBER 9: Cooper Flagg #32 of the Dallas Mavericks goes to the basket during the first half against the Indiana Pacers at American Airlines Center on November 9, 2026 in Dallas, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images) | Getty Images

As good (and fun) as the Mavs have been early on, Irving knows his team still has a long way to go to get to the level they want to be at.

"We haven't earned anything in this league yet," Irving said. "We consistently do it every night, and that's how you build your identity in this league and you earn your respect. We try not to put the cart before the horse."

With that being said, though, Mavs fans have earned the right to enjoy this start and, dare I say, dream big again. After two years of nothing but gut punches, a 7-4 start built on a generational teenager, a healthy veteran star and a team that genuinely seems to like playing together is a foundation Mavs fans have been waiting on.

Irving acknowledged the preseason doubt, saying the team heard "a lot of the noise" and chose not to let outside voices into the locker room. If he keeps playing like prime Kyrie, though, and if Flagg keeps rewriting the record books at this current pace, those voices of doubt are going to continue to get a whole lot quieter.

The Mavericks will now hit the road for a big three-game trip that will show just how real this start is, beginning Thursday against the Minnesota Timberwolves at Target Center at 7 p.m. CT. Dallas then visits the Cleveland Cavaliers on Nov. 14 and the Boston Celtics on Nov. 15.

#2769. Views from the Game: Rockets defeat Nuggets 110-100; TDS speaks with Kevin Durant, Alperen Sengun

The Houston Rockets faced the Denver Nuggets in unfamiliar territory on Monday. The Rockets entered Monday night's game on their first two-game losing streak of the season after their 102-99 loss to the Phoenix Suns on Saturday.

In that game, the Rockets struggled from the field as the Suns led by double digits in the first quarter. The Rockets eventually got back in the game and even took a six-point lead at one point in the second half. Still, even a fourth-quarter resurgence from Alperen Sengun, who struggled the first three quarters, wasn't enough to keep the Rockets from dropping their second straight game.

The Rockets welcomed the Nuggets, who are coming off a win down in Mexico City over the Los Angeles Clippers. The Rockets have been without Steven Adams and Clint Capela for several games and also added Oscar Tshiebwe to their injury report with an illness. That means the Rockets will be without all three of their backup centers, leaving Sengun as the only active center for Monday's game.

Ime Udoka did mention how both Steven Adams and Clint Capela are targeting the upcoming road trip, specifically the Washington and Miami games, as possible return dates. That would be a welcome sight for a Rockets team that currently ranks 12th in rebounding after being near or at the top every season of Ime Udoka's Rockets tenure.

The Rockets got off to a fast start, led by Durant, who made his first three shots, including one from beyond the arc. Durant was as aggressive in the first quarter as he has been in several games. The quarter was back and forth, as neither team could get much separation.

The Nuggets started to take advantage of the Rockets' lack of depth at center as Jokic went to work once Sengun went to the bench. However, the Rockets put together a good finish to the quarter, and a Tari Eason 3-pointer put them up 32-24 at the end of the first quarter. Durant led all scorers with 11 points in the first 12 minutes.

The Rockets carried that momentum into the second quarter, scoring the first 11 points and building a lead of as much as 19. The Rockets played with much more force and composure than in their first half against the Suns. The Rockets had 13 assists out of their first 20 made baskets. The Rockets maintained the lead, taking a 54-40 lead into halftime.

The third quarter saw the Nuggets cut the lead to under double digits early as they started the quarter on fire from the field. The Rockets, meanwhile, saw their shooting fall off a cliff, starting 2-for-14 from the field as the Nuggets came back from an early 18-point deficit to tie the game at 5:02.

That's when Marcus Smart and Tari Eason entered the game, and the Rockets' defensive intensity immediately rose. The Rockets strung together good defensive possessions that led to easy baskets and pushed the lead back to nine at 71-62. Despite a rough start to the quarter, the Rockets led 77-68 heading into the fourth quarter.

In the fourth quarter, both teams played at a high level for the first time. On one end, Sengun scored in the paint; on the other, Jamal Murray could not miss from mid-range. The Rockets had a slim six-point lead midway through the fourth quarter.

That's when Sengun took over: he not only scored in the paint to give the Rockets a 98-90 lead, but he also assisted on the next two baskets, helping the Rockets put the game away with a 110-100 win. The win snapped the Rockets' first two-game losing streak of the season.

After the game, Ime Udoka, Kevin Durant, and Alperen Sengun spoke to the media. Udoka said the Rockets did a much better job taking care of the basketball and distributing it, and that they finished with 29 assists. SB Nation asked Durant whether it is easier to figure out the defense when he's initiating the offense.

Sengun helped close out the Nuggets with his own great passing and running the pick-and-roll with Durant. Here are both players praising each other's games after last night's win.

The Rockets now begin preparing for their old nemesis, Steph Curry and the Golden State Warriors, who come to town Wednesday with an 8-3 record and have won their last eight games.

#2765. What We Learned from the Spurs win over the Suns

It's hard not to feel like you're watching a mirage during some of these games. The level of play is excellent and the bits and pieces you might be tempted to pick at are scarce. The wins are piling up. The vibes are good. Everything is going according to plan. Nothing to see here…right?

Right! Look, I'm not going to even try to play devil's advocate here. No one wants to be the guy pointing at the Alien dropping 40 and 11 over 25 minutes and saying, "actually, this is bad." If that's a take you'd like to read then I can assure the internet is full of people willing to take you up on the offer. For my part, and if you've come to this website today, I'm assuring you, I genuinely find it hard to think of a less interesting angle to come at this from.

Victor Wembanyama is simply brilliant. He's been brilliant, he's brilliant now, and he only seems to be getting more brillianter as we go along. Twelve of his fifteen made shots on Monday were dunks or layups, and nine of those were dunks. Four different teammates threw him an alley-oop. The Spurs are running a dizzying array of different motions that all end up at the same destination, which is a Wembanyama dunk. The threes, instead of feeling like something he has to do to open up the lane, now just arrive in the natural rhythm of the game. He made two threes all night, a digestif tacked on at the end of a satisfying meal.

Vic even hit a Dream Shake in the middle of the 2nd quarter that left me staring off in the distance in disbelief.

I sometimes try to avoid writing about the Victor Wembanyama of it all when I do these because it feels too easy. What did we learn from the Spurs win? They still have the best player on the planet and he helps a lot. Case closed. To his credit, he goes out of his way to make ignoring him next to impossible.

The problem, if there is one, is that regular season basketball does actually seem easy for him at this point. That's not a mirage. I have no doubt about how hard he's worked to achieve the level he's currently operating on, but that doesn't change the fact that watching him dismantle the average NBA team every other night doesn't look very challenging. He's like Will Hunting ranting at Professor Lambeau about how easy it is to solve those supposedly impossible graph theory equations.

Victor's ascension this season is impressive, and I want to do my best to appreciate the casual brilliance we are privy to on a regular basis, but that greatness comes at a cost, and that cost is a raised ceiling. I simply don't care that he can drop 50 on the Mavs or 40 on the Suns. I don't care that he can snuff out the Blazers. I'm sure there will be another jaw-dropping stat line on Wednesday when he plays the Bulls, and I'm sure it will be met with another polite nod from me.

None of this is his fault, mind you. The schedule is the schedule and the teams are the teams. He's taking care of business, and that's all you can really ask of him.

I guess I've just spent the last nine games of this winning streak telling myself I still don't know what I'm looking at and I really believe anyone who tells you they do is lying. The ease with which they are winning these games is real. Every conclusion we draw from it…well, that's a little more hazy. I try to grab on to things I know. "The Spurs are Good." "The Suns are Bad." "Wemby is Tall," and project out from there but I end up feeling like I'm chasing the ghost of a conclusion. The idea of a resolution instead of an actual one.

This is a champagne problem at most. Like, what, I'm having a bad time because I can't tell if the Spurs are great, really great, or generationally amazing? A few years ago we were sitting through a sixteen-game losing streak and then an eighteen-game one, on our way to the lottery again and again. Now I'm hemming and hawing because our first brush with success last spring has got me feeling antsy.

The thing I'm dancing around here is that the Finals loss is an albatross around our necks that we're just going to have to wear. There's no two ways about it. I'm encouraged by the things I'm seeing from this new three-guard- Hydra, but I won't feel comfortable until I know it can outscore Jalen Brunson when he's going Nuclear. I love that Victor seems more calm and assured in his decision making, but I still have nightmares about KAT finding a way to neutralize him. Every time we race out to a lead this season, my brain remembers the blown leads in June.

The context of the past clouds everything from the present and I don't think there's an easy fix for that feeling. It shouldn't sully our enjoyment of the current moment, but it does ground the results in a certain reality.

All of this is certainly real enough, but none of it really matters.

I don't feel qualified to talk about what Dylan Harper is doing. It's a level of basketball that I recognize as great but have difficulty quantifying, because my analysis tends to err on the side of "oh my God, how did he do that?" Nuance exits the room when he has the ball in his hands. There is a grace and fluidity to his game that is hypnotic, whether he's getting to the basket with relative ease or casually spinning into a midrange jumper. I don't know how to say this as a compliment, but it's fascinatingly boring to watch. He's operating at breakneck speed but still in complete control, sort of like how F1 cars can look a little blah during a race until you blink and realize they're going like 200 mph.

The caveat with Dylan is, obviously, his youth. It's simultaneously the most exciting and frustrating thing about him. That control I just alluded to can prove elusive sometimes. Sometimes he seems almost like he's just watching the game happen to him and forgets that he's more than capable of grabbing the reins. He started the game last night a little bit adrift. Whether that's a byproduct of the three-guard lineup's growing pains or him simply sitting back and watching Wemby cook like the rest of us, he was kind of invisible, and a guy like Harper just shouldn't be invisible. I love the way he fits into the similar but different skill sets of our guards, and he seems a little more freed up now that Harper and Castle can take on more responsibility. He's still so fast and he still has great vision, and last night he finished with 15 points, six assists and nine rebounds. His chemistry with Wembanyama has only gotten better, with four of those six assists going to Wemby, and their propensity for lobs and oops of all types seems to have rubbed off on everyone around them. The Minnesota Vikings lost their second game in a row on Monday, as they were defeated by the Buffalo Bills 23-6. The defense held up their end of the bargain, limiting Josh Allen and James Cook for most of the night, but were let down once again by the offense. #2760. Draymond Green states potential Jordan Poole-Warriors reunion a ‘non-issue'

Draymond Green states potential Jordan Poole-Warriors reunion a 'non-issue' originally appeared on NBC Sports Bay Area

Three seasons and 11 games have passed since Jordan Poole has played for the Warriors.

Despite the ugly conflict with Draymond Green that precipitated his exit, Poole said after the Warriors' win Monday over his New Orleans Pelicans that he would consider returning "home" to the team that drafted him in 2019.

Considering the nature of that incident, it would be fair to ask if Green would have an issue playing alongside Poole again.

"I have no issue with that at all," Green said in the locker room after the game, according to Bay Area News Group's Joseph Dycus. "I will never stand in the way of this organization thinking they can better themselves."

Seeing those last two quoted sentences in social media posts, many fans speculated that Green was inferring Poole would be the one to have an issue with a reunion.

Green, on his podcast "The Draymond Green Show," clarified his postgame comments, pointing out that any decision regarding a Poole-Warriors reunion comes down to the organizations, and not himself.

"What those comments were — they asked me about Jordan Poole's comments … and they were asking me, like, how did I feel about that," Green recalled on his podcast. "And I told them I don't have a problem with that at all. Number one, I don't make decisions here. I'm a basketball player. I don't decide my own future here, let alone someone else's …

"Number two, what I said was also, I'm an adult. So if you're asking me as if that's going to be a problem for me, that's no problem for me … I'm not someone who walks around with a grudge."

The San Francisco Standard's Danny Emerman provided another quote from Green from Monday night, in which the Warriors veteran further explained how he has moved on from the incident, and that the decision around Poole returning does not fall on him.

"We had our issue that I f–ked up on, and that's that," Green said, according to Emerman. "But I'm not one to hold grudges, I'm not one to sit around and try to damper something for someone else. So if that's what he wants, I understand that.

"But that's not a Draymond issue. That's a Golden State Warriors decision."

In his podcast, Green provided an example of a similar situation, saying that Warriors general manager Mike Dunleavy asked him about his thoughts on trading for then-Washington Wizards guard Chris Paul. Green recalled that he told his GM that the two did not see "eye-to-eye" and that he couldn't say that he was "very fond of him at all."

"I told Mike then — I said, 'Mike, I wouldn't stand in the way of what you think this team needs, or what can help make this team better,'" Green recalled telling Dunleavy. "I would never stand in the way of that. And so, same went for last night when I was asked that …

"… If they were like, 'Man, we're bringing Jordan Poole in' — whether that's a trade, whatever it is — and I was still [with the Warriors], that's a non-issue for me."

Green seems to be abstinent when it comes to personnel decisions at this point in his career, and that extends to any possible reunion with Poole.

BOULDER, Colo. (AP) — Colorado sophomore Ian Inman scored 26 points on 8-for-13 shooting from 3-point range and the Buffaloes beat San Diego 83-75 on Tuesday night.

Barrington Hargress scored 16 points, reserve Josiah Sanders 15 and Noah Feddersen 10. Alex Dickeson grabbed 10 rebounds for Colorado (2-1).

Davion Hill scored 20 points, Jevon Hill 18 and Dusty Stromer 11 for the Toreros (2-1).

#2752. Jimmy Butler’s hysterical ‘coaching’ debut draws wild reaction in 51-point win: ‘He trippin’

Coffee connoisseur. Domino don. Coach Jimmy?

Jimmy Butler has no shortage of hobbies and side gigs to keep him busy even while unable to get on the court for the Warriors while rehabbing the ACL he tore in January. He added another Monday night, to the amusement of his Golden State teammates.

At least one of them would prefer to see Butler stick to his dayjob(s), though.

"Man, nah, nah, nah. He gotta go home," Warriors guard De'Anthony Melton told the NBC Sports Bay Area broadcast following the 138-87 win over the Pelicans. "The next time he do something like that, he gotta go back home or do something else. Because he trippin'."

De'Anthony Melton of the Golden State Warriors speaks to the media after a game against the New Orleans Pelicans on Monday, Nov. 9, 2026, in San Francisco. NBAE via Getty Images

Melton was on the receiving end of Butler's most pointed coaching advice of the night.

Taking his usual seat on the bench, Butler traded in his typically fashion-forward wardrobe for a white pullover and black joggers — the same get-up as Steve Kerr and the rest of the Warriors coaching staff. He also grabbed a clipboard, which came in handy to remind Melton of the golden rule of basketball in Golden State: Pass the ball to Steph Curry.

When Melton checked out midway through the third quarter, Butler spelled it out loud and clear in blue ink on the clipboard and held it up for Melton — and the cameras — to see.

Georges Niang, left, and Jimmy Butler III smile after a game at Chase Center in San Francisco, Monday, Nov. 9, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images

Melton had just violated the one and only edict on two possessions in quick succession. Curry was open on the perimeter but Melton drove to the rim through traffic and failed to convert.

Butler offered him — and the rest of the Warriors — a simple reminder.

"All I learned is once you're on the court with Steph, give Steph the ball," rookie Yaxel Lendeborg said of Butler as a tactician. "Just get the ball to Steph. That's the most serious thing he said."

Stephen Curry (30) of the Golden State Warriors prepares to shoot against the New Orleans Pelicans on Monday, Nov. 9, 2026, in San Francisco. Getty Images

Butler gave his teammates no advance notice of his plans for the game. Lendeborg even mistook him for a regular member of the coaching staff at first.

"I think it was during the first timeout. I was walking by, going to ask coach Frank (Vogel) a question and I see Jimmy. Like, what? What are you wearing?" Lendeborg chuckled. "I didn't realize all the coaches wear the same thing until today."

Butler's wardrobe ensured that he would blend right in on the bench.

"I thought he looked great. Really good-looking sweater," Kerr quipped. "He said all the right things. Team fouls. How many team fouls we had. He was really acting the part. But I also realized he was mocking us, so it hurt a little bit."

It was all in good fun, but Melton agreed: he preferred Butler on the court than the bench.

"No. Just no," Melton said with a laugh when asked about Butler's coaching debut. "I think he just got fired today, which is actually crazy. I'm happy about that."

The Breisgau outfit had to work hard to break down a defensive-minded Union side at the Europa-Park Stadion, but second-half goals from Rani Khedira (OG) and Yuito Suzuki ensured they claimed all three points.

Speaking to Sportschau after the match, Schuster expressed his satisfaction with how his players carried out their game plan, particularly their ability to remain patient while waiting for opportunities.

“The joy is very great. Because we managed to implement what we had planned. It was clear that we needed patience. We showed that,” Schuster explained.

The Freiburg coach also highlighted the importance of maintaining belief in their own quality, even when clear-cut opportunities were difficult to come by.

“Maintaining belief, trusting our own quality and waiting for the right moments, even when they don’t come in great numbers. That was very disciplined,” he added.

Schuster was particularly pleased with the togetherness shown by his players, acknowledging that matches against opponents who prioritise defensive organisation can become frustrating.

“It can be frustrating, but it shouldn’t be. That is exactly the quality. Games like these can get into your head. It was important that the boys were there for each other,” he continued.

The Freiburg coach also praised the mutual understanding within his squad, describing the collective support between his players as something that was particularly pleasing to observe.

Defender Matthias Ginter echoed his coach’s assessment, having made his 200th Bundesliga appearance for Freiburg during Sunday’s victory.

“It’s generally never a walk in the park against Union Berlin,” Ginter told Sportschau, acknowledging the physical challenge posed by the visitors.

The experienced defender also pointed towards lessons learned from previous encounters with Union, explaining that Freiburg needed to remain committed to their approach rather than take unnecessary risks.

“It was important that we added the second goal and also hardly allowed anything,” Ginter explained.

The victory represents Freiburg’s fourth consecutive win in all competitions and moves them up to third place in the Bundesliga standings with 19 points after nine matches.

#2737. Five Plays: Georgia Tech First Quarter

Brian Brohm got things going on the very first play of the game. Louisville needed to spread the ball around more, and they needed to get the tight ends involved. The motion with Tre Richardson to draw eyes, followed by play action, was a perfect way to get Jaleel Skinner open across the middle of the field.

Lincoln Keiholz also does a very good job of staying patient as the GT outside linebacker drops into the path of this throw. Linc simply holds the ball until Skinner clears and delivers a nice ball that allows him to get up the field for a big play to start the game.

Louisville's defense also set the tone early on their first snap of the game. GT uses motion, which UofL has had fits with, but Jabari Mack and Koen Entringer are in solid position after the snap to at least make a quick tackle on a completion. It shouldn't be this way, but it is very nice to see guys execute their assignment after the motion.

The guy who makes the play on this one is Tyler Thompson. He does a great job on his inside rush to make Alberto Mendoza move his feet. As soon as he gets the snap, he has Thompson in his line of sight, and by the time he turns to make this throw, Thompson is close enough that he has to move. The timing is completely off from the jump, and the Cards get a sack.

Louisville spent this game getting Stanquan Clark downhill against the run. He timed up the snap a handful of times, and if he didn't make the tackle, he at least made the running back stop his feet and adjust. As you see here, his running start makes it really easy for him to blow by the left tackle, who barely gets a hand on him.

Josh Donald also does a great job of firing off the ball to beat the left guard across his face. The defense set the tone early, and I truly believe it was a key factor in how they played all game.

TreyShun Hurry is a completely different player than he was last season. He was used on a handful of throws down the sideline, and he barely looked like a guy who could play at the FBS level when he got those opportunities. This route is exactly what you want to see from a Power 4 receiver. It's how you coach it, and more than that, it's how you want it executed in the moment.

Hurry starts this off with a great split in how he lines up. He's at the numbers, so he has plenty of room to run this route with speed. If he were further outside, he would need to make a move at the line to get even with the defensive back. He angles to the sideline at the snap because he has space to do so, then he works to get even and then get by the corner. He starts handfighting as soon as he gets to an even point, and while doing so, he uses his speed to get ahead of the corner. He finishes it off with an impressive catch through contact. Really good stuff here.

Brian Brohm was in his bag to start this game. He's down inside the 10, so it's likely GT will be in man coverage. He calls a simple play to get his fast guy on the edge of the defense, where he is running away from coverage. The defender in coverage doesn't react to the motion from Tre Richardson, and it's an easy natural pick to get him wide open for an easy touchdown. I'd imagine Brian called this a touchdown in the booth before the ball was snapped.

Ben Perry makes a great play here. I have noticed over the last few weeks that Perry, or whoever is in at the time, will blitz or at least get tight to the line of scrimmage and get downhill when there is not a receiver to their side. However, they have also done so when there is a receiver, which has led to some easy passes.

I like the overall mindset, because it leads to plays like this one, where you essentially have a defender who is unaccounted for. Perry is lined up a few yards off the ball as everyone initially lines up. But he creeps up to the line and gets on the ball so quickly that he is no longer the option read. He makes the choice for the quarterback because he is right there at the point where he would hand it off or keep it. The aggressive approach has been the answer all season. I'll keep shouting it into the ether.

The offensive line has been better than as of late, but this type of mistake is really concerning as the Cards look to back their way into the ACC championship game. Pitt will feast if the line can't get their calls right, as we see here. This is a very basic pressure from GT, and it looks like they just don't communicate responsibilities very well.

Cason Henry is the guy I'm focused on at right tackle, because he doesn't have any reason to let a defensive end get a free rush here unless he thinks there is a running back to pick him up. The basic rule against a blitz is to take the inside threat, but the line is not outnumbered on this play. What should happen is that the center would pick up the blitzer, and everyone else takes the man in front of them. Henry blocks down, and you end up with three blockers for two players. Not a big deal in this game, as this was the only blown pass block, but better defenses will look to do this all game long.

That division is on fire and so far New England has an 0-2 (Bears, Packers) against them. It's hard to try and sugarcoat the tough task ahead for the Pats in Week 10. The injured list grew last week and the team will be without two more starters in Ben Brown and Rhamondre Stevenson. The Lions are favored by 2.5 points, which seems low considering the state of the patchwork roster. Frankly, I would be happy to see a good solid effort all around. Hoping for a win, but not feeling too confident unless the offense can limit turnovers and the defense can return to form after a bad week. There's always a chance.

#2732. Believe it, Lakers are NBA championship contenders

Luka Dončić is playing as though he's on a revenge tour and every opposing player has former Mavericks general manager Nico Harrison's face superimposed on it.

Austin Reaves is playing as though he were shortchanged by signing a four-year, $180 million deal over the summer, the richest contract in NBA history for a player who went undrafted.

Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic (77) shoots against Atlanta Hawks guard CJ McCollum during an NBA game, Monday, Nov. 9, 2026, in Atlanta. AP Photo/Mike Stewart

Walker Kessler is playing as though he's hellbent on fulfilling his vow to "run through a wall" for the Lakers after they emptied their treasure trove of draft capital to acquire him in July.

And the Lakers' role players are playing as though they deeply understood the assignment when they joined a 17-time championship franchise.

The Lakers have the league's best record at 10-2. They've won six games in a row.

That isn't a sentence we thought we'd write heading into this season. Not with nine new players. Not with so many question marks around their perimeter defense. Not with their lack of depth at backup center.

But now, Lakers general manager Rob Pelinka looks like the Albert Einstein of basketball rosters and coach JJ Redick looks like a superstar whisperer.

The Lakers last won a championship in 2020, their first title in 10 years.

They could snap their six-year drought this season.

Dončić is on a historic tear, averaging 39.3 points (49.8% shooting from the field, 40.7% from beyond the arc), 7.8 rebounds, 7.9 assists and two steals per game.

In his first nine games of the season, Dončić scored 361 points, surpassing Michael Jordan's 347 points in 1986-87 for the most points scored through that period in modern NBA history.

But what really made the Lakers look like contenders is how they played without Dončić (lower back tightness) on Sunday against the Pistons.

Austin Reaves (15) of the Los Angeles Lakers reacts after a late second-half 3-point basket against the Detroit Pistons in Detroit, Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Getty Images

Without the league's current front-runner for the MVP Award and against a Pistons team with the third-highest defensive rating, Reaves scored a season-high 43 points in the Lakers' 121-116 win.

He reminded everyone of what he can do when he's unleashed.

Reaves has quietly been putting together a spectacular season. He's averaging 25.3 points on a very efficient 50.8% from the field and 41.3% from beyond the arc.

He's the 15th leading scorer in the league, and of those ahead of him, only Giannis Antetokounmpo, Anthony Davis and Victor Wembanyama have higher field-goal percentages than Reaves.

And only Jamal Murray and Steph Curry are shooting at a higher percentage from beyond the 3-point line.

Dončić and Reaves are the NBA's highest-scoring duo by a mile, averaging 64.6 points, 12.6 more than the second-leading duo of Steph Curry and Yaxel Lendeborg, who are averaging a combined 52 points per game.

Then there's Kessler, who's averaging a double-double with 14.9 points and 10.8 rebounds per game.

When Reaves was out for Monday's 124-114 win over the Hawks because of an illness, Dončić got help from the Lakers' reserves, with Collin Sexton having an 18-point, six-assist performance and Sandro Mamukelashvili pouring in 23 points and grabbing eight rebounds.

Los Angeles Lakers center Walker Kessler (14) shoots against Atlanta Hawks center Jock Landale (31) during an NBA basketball game, Monday, Nov. 9, 2026, in Atlanta. AP Photo/Mike Stewart

The Lakers have the highest offensive rating in the league at 121.5. And even though they're 19th in defensive rating (113.8), they rank second in the league in steals per game (10.8), second in total deflections (240) and third in blocks per game (6.4).

Kessler leads the NBA in contested shots (140).

Heck, even Dončić, who has notoriously been slammed for his defense throughout his career, is showing a lot of effort on the less glamorous end of the court. He leads the league in defensive loose balls recovered (nine) and is tied for second in charges drawn (four).

Entering this season, it was presumed that the Lakers needed time to jell. It seemed as though they had major holes. They weren't ready to compete with the league's elite teams, such as the Thunder, Spurs or Knicks.

The Lakers have sprinted past their doubters, proving that they're a team to watch.

#2731. Cardinals place QB Gardner Minshew and WR Michael Wilson on IR

The Cardinals placed quarterback Gardner Minshew and wide receiver Michael Wilson on injured reserve Tuesday, the team announced.

Minshew tore the UCL in his elbow and will miss the rest of the season. Wilson’s neck injury will end his season.

“Not the ending I had envisioned, but grateful for the journey,” Wilson wrote on social media. “Regardless of what happens, my love for the game will never change! Thank you for all the love and support. The story is still being written.”

Wilson played eight games in 2026, making 51 receptions for 546 yards and two touchdowns.

In two appearances, Minshew completed 38 of 53 passes for 354 yards and three touchdowns, and led the Cardinals to an overtime win in Dallas in Week 8. He is scheduled to be a free agent at the end of the season.

The Cardinals signed veteran quarterback Josh Johnson and rookie quarterback Joey Aguilar to back up rookie Carson Beck. Beck will get his first NFL start on Sunday against the Rams.

Aguilar was on the Jaguars’ practice squad, and Johnson was on the Bengals’ practice squad.

The Cardinals also signed receiver Phillip Dorsett II to the practice squad and released tight end Rivaldo Fairweather and running back Jermar Jefferson from the practice squad.

#2730. Heat end trip with shaky victory over Jazz

SALT LAKE CITY – Against another opponent on another night, the Miami Heat's momentum might have stalled. Instead the perfect opponent to end a five-game, 10-day trip.

Against a team that entered 1-9 and was without four of five starters, the Heat made it three victories in their last four games with a 115-109 victory Tuesday night over the Utah Jazz at Delta Center.

While it wasn't as easy as expected, and while the record still is underwater at 5-6, the victory completed a 3-2 western swing for Erik Spoelstra's team, with a five-game homestand to follow.

Not only did the Jazz enter with the league's worst record, but they were without starters Keyonte George, Jaren Jackson Jr., Lauri Markkanen and Jusuf Nurkic.

So while it was somewhat shaky, the Heat did (barely) enough, even with Giannis Antetokounmpo battling an ongoing wrist issue and this time foul trouble, as well.

With Antetokounmpo still working his way to 30 points and 11 rebounds, the Heat had enough against an opponent that got 25 points from No. 2 2026 draft pick Darryn Peterson and 23 from Ace Baily.

In support of Antetokounmpo, the Heat got 19 points, eight assists and five rebounds from Davion Mitchell, on a night Bam Adebayo was held to 11 points along with eight rebounds.

Five degrees of Heat from Tuesday night's game:

— Game flow: The Heat led 29-25 after the first period. They then pushed their lead to 17 in the second period, and then went into halftime up 64-54, unable to build more of a lead despite 11 first-half Jazz turnovers.

The Jazz then trimmed their deficit to six early in the third period, before the Heat pushed their lead to 85-66 on an Antetokounmpo 3-pointer midway through the third, going up 23, before taking a 92-72 into the fourth.

From there, though, the Jazz moved within 101-93 with 6:42 to play on consecutive Isaiah Collier 3-pointers.

That is when Antetokounmpo settled the offense, as the Heat mostly settled the game, aided by a Klay Thompson chase-down block when the Jazz threatened to close within five with 65 seconds to play.

And even then, it required another transition block, this time by Adebayo, when the Jazz threatened to close within three with 22.1 seconds to play.

— Waiting game: Antetokounmpo had been downgraded from probable to questionable 90 minutes before tip due to his sprained right wrist that has been taped postgame recently.

Then, an hour before tip, the Heat announced Antetokounmpo was good to go.

Of the initial indecision, Spoelstra said, "We just have to evaluate where he is, just like we would with anybody else."

The calculus with Antetokounmpo nonetheless changed when he was called for his second foul with 5:33 left in the opening period, forcing Adebayo to quickly return amid his first rest of the night.

Antetokounmpo then iced his wrist while on the bench.

Antetokounmpo then was called for his third foul with 6:33 left in the second period, a call Spoelstra unsuccessfully challenged, nonetheless leaving Antetokounmpo in the game at that stage.

With his eighth point, Antetokounmpo passed Gary Payton (21,813) for 39th place on the NBA all-time scoring list.

Antetokounmpo closed 12 of 21 from the field, 5 of 9 from the line, with free throws remaining an ongoing Heat issue.

— More change: The Heat for the second consecutive game played with Pelle Larsson as their starting small forward, with Andrew Wiggins therefore playing his second game of the season off the bench.

The recent changes continued further down the rotation, with Ryan Conwell playing ahead of Tim Hardaway Jr.

Wiggins entered midway through the opening period.

The rotational realignment then continued at the top of the second period, when Myron Gardner and Simone Fontecchio entered, as Hardaway remained planted on the bench.

Wiggins closed with 13 points, Conwell with five, Gardner with four and Fontecchio with three.

— Rough go: Adebayo opened 0 for 6 from the field, at one point early in the third period with four fouls and six points.

The Jazz continually offered Adebayo open outside attempts, including a pair of wayward 3-point shots.

Adebayo did not convert his first basket until 8:12 remained, when he converted an 11-foot jumper to move to 1 of 7, on the way to his 1 of 8 close.

— Onward: Up next for the Heat is a five-game homestand that opens with a Friday-Saturday back-to-back set against the Cleveland Cavaliers and then Detroit Pistons. The Heat are not on the road again until Nov. 25 against the Philadelphia 76ers, the day before Thanksgiving.

Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers elaborated on his issues with comments made about him during last Sunday’s Fox broadcast during a press conference on Tuesday.

Fox announcers Joe Davis, Greg Olsen, and Pam Oliver discussed Nabers’s body language at several points during the game and shots of an agitated Nabers on the sideline were shown multiple times. Davis was particularly critical about Nabers’s response to a touchdown by teammate Isaiah Likely and Olsen said in response that “there’s a very fine line between being demanding, being a competitor, and all those great things” before adding that Nabers has “just got to keep it in check.”

“I just feel like the narrative on me is always all the bad body language things that people have been saying about me,” Nabers said, via a transcript from the team. “But as far as that, if it’s a problem with anybody, the cameras can stay off me. The thing about it is, don’t tell the world something that’s not me. I’m [going to] speak up for myself all the time because there’s nobody else that’s going to be able to speak up for me. So, I’m going to use my own voice and be able to speak up about me being a bad teammate. And I felt like that was just a lie, just attacking my character as a football player and as a teammate. Like I said, I’ve never been on a team where anyone has called me a bad teammate that I know of.”

Olsen took issue with the incorrect quotes about Nabers being a bad teammate and the wideout was asked if he’s heard from directly from him since Sunday. Nabers said he hasn’t, but “he can reach out and we can have a simple conversation.” Beyond that, Nabers said he’s done talking about the subject and that he’s moved on to Thursday’s game against the Commanders.

#2728. Collin Sexton has focused on patience as he tries to find role with Lakers

Over the past two games, Collin Sexton has been indispensable in powering the Los Angeles Lakers to wins with their star guards, Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves, each missing one contest.

Against the Detroit Pistons on Sunday, the veteran guard tallied 17 points (5-of-10 shooting), two assists and two rebounds. A day later, he followed that up with 18 points (6-of-11 shooting), six assists, two rebounds and one steal in Monday's win over the Atlanta Hawks.

If those consecutive performances are any indication, Sexton could be finding his footing after a slow start to 2026-27, which featured a calf strain that hampered him during training camp and preseason.

Through his first nine appearances, he averaged 8.7 points while shooting 40% from the floor and 25.8% from deep (49.5% true shooting). In this week's pair of victories, he's averaged 17.5 points on 52.4% shooting and 50% from deep (64.4% true shooting). Following those laudatory outings, Sexton said he feels he's inching closer to fully being himself again.

"I think maybe another week and a half, two weeks and I think I'll be back," he told reporters Monday. "Right now, these last two games felt really good. So I'm moving in the right direction."

As Sexton works to rediscover his rhythm, he's embracing patience.

"That's one word I've been using each and every day," he said. "I would say each and every day is going to have its ups, have its downs but I'm blessed to be healthy enough to go out."

Head coach JJ Redick is counting on Sexton to help steady second units for the Lakers, given he's their most talented scorer and qualified initiator off the bench. After Monday's win, he spoke about Sexton's role in keeping the offense humming when the speedy guard is at the forefront.

"I think the biggest thing [is] we're trying to get organized and and there's glimpses of really good organization when he's out there as the primary ball handler," Redick told reporters. "We got a little squirrely there at the end of the second quarter. I thought, for the most part, outside of the first few minutes in that third quarter where I had to call the early timeout, I thought we did a good job of just being organized and trying to get good shots. That's how you end up with 124 points against a good team."

#2725. Game Preview: Phoenix aims to bounce back vs. Clippers

Who: Phoenix Suns (3-6) vs. Los Angeles Clippers (2-7)

Where: Mortgage Matchup Center — Phoenix, Arizona

The Phoenix Suns will need to have a short memory after being dominated by Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs last night.

Wemby walked into our building and dropped 40, 11, and nine blocks in 25 minutes without breaking a sweat. Spurs 122, Suns 96. It was a rough night. But the silver lining is that the starters were on the bench with 9:34 left. Because tonight they have the second of a back-to-back, and tired legs cannot be an excuse.

The mood in this fanbase right now is somewhere between "burn it down" and "it's November, relax." The Suns sit at 3-6. They're 2-2 on this seven-game homestand. The two-game win streak over Houston and Orlando either becomes a distant memory (after a loss) or a building block if they win, because then it's suddenly "they've won 3 of their last 4 games". So which is it?

Make no mistake about it… this is a MUST-WIN game for the Suns. These are the teams you need to beat.

Ingram and Beal are still out, so expect LA to run back the same five that started Sunday in their win over the Pelicans.

Mark Williams — OUT (Left Shoulder Surgery)

Devin Booker needs help, and he needs it from the starters.

Book went 10-for-17 for 32 last night. The other four starters combined for 27 points on 10-of-36 shooting. That's 27.8%. Phoenix shot 39.3% as a team. Jalen Green, Dillon Brooks and Miles Bridges have to be the second and third options tonight, or this turns into another Booker solo show that ends in a loss.

LA snapped a seven-game skid Sunday by beating New Orleans 139-123, and the bench won that game: 59 points and 14 assists from the reserves. Gradey Dick went 6-for-7. Top-5 pick Keaton Wagler hit 3 of 4 from deep in 18 minutes. Wagler also picked up five fouls. That unit is 4th in bench scoring per game, but defensively they have some flaws. Attack, attack, attack.

Darius Garland went for 24 and 10 against the Pelicans. Brook Lopez added 20. Brandon Ingram (heel) and Bradley Beal (knee) are both out tonight. Gillespie, Goodwin and Green have to make Garland work on the ball, and whoever draws Lopez has to drag him out to the perimeter, where his feet are slow.

Rebounding is going to be the key for every Suns game, as the Spurs outrebounded them by twenty, 55 to 35.

LA shot 55% from the field (46 of 84), went 16-for-38 from three, and piled up 34 assists against 11 turnovers in their win over the Pelicans. They lived at the line, too: 31 of 38 from the line while the Pelicans committed 29 fouls. The glass was basically even, 36-35 Clippers, with LA grabbing 13 offensive boards.

The starters held serve, every one of them finishing between +2 and +9. The bench blew it open. Max Strus and Gradey Dick were both +17, Kobe Sanders was +15, and Keaton Wagler was +11. LA won the fourth quarter 37-28.

Collin Gillespie, anyone? It's been a rough season for him, and boy could they use a breakout game in this one from him, not only for his confidence, but to outduel the Clippers' bench. Jordan Goodwin is back as well, so that hopefully provides a spark.

Do not take them lightly. The Clippers are 2nd in the NBA in 3PT% and 4th in bench scoring. Despite their flaws and 7-game losing streak, they are fully capable of getting hot from deep and stealing this one.

The Suns bounce back, and their offense breaks out in a win over the Clippers. We enter the 10-game mark at 4-6, with mixed reviews, but ultimately trending in the right direction, winning 3 of 4.

#2723. Celtics roll past the 76ers 123-101 as Paul George pours in 36 in Philly return

PHILADELPHIA (AP) — Jayson Tatum scored 21 points and outplayed former Boston teammate Jaylen Brown, and Paul George hit six 3-pointers and scored 36 points in his return to Philadelphia, leading the Celtics past the 76ers 123-101 on Tuesday night.

Brown ran into early foul trouble and scored only 13 points in his first game against Boston since the 2024 NBA Finals MVP was traded over the summer to the Sixers. His head-to-head showdown with Tatum was one of the more anticipated early-season matchups with both players refusing to say much about their frosty relationship.

Tatum tried to dap up Brown before the opening tip with a tap on the shoulder and thump on the chest that his former teammate ignored. Tatum shook hands and exchanged a big hug with LeBron James.

Brown picked up two quick fouls in the first quarter and was whistled for his fourth early in the second half.

George, traded for Brown after two seasons with the 76ers, enjoyed the homecoming. He appeared to give the finger in a bowling motion near the visitor's bench after he sank his fourth 3 of the game for a 100-82 lead that pushed the Celtics to their ninth win in 10 games.

The Sixers survived a scare late in the second half when Joel Embiid landed awkwardly and hit the court on a missed layup attempt. The oft-injured big man curled up on the court while VJ Edgecombe dunked over him.

NEW YORK (AP) — Jalen Brunson scored 23 points, Karl-Anthony Towns had 21 points and 16 rebounds, and New York beat Milwaukee for its fourth straight victory.

OG Anunoby made five 3-pointers and finished with 19 points for the Knicks, who have won six of seven since an 0-3 start. They outscored the Bucks 32-13 in the second quarter to blow open the game and then put it away in the fourth after Milwaukee had gotten back into it.

The Knicks got big efforts from their bench, with no starter playing more than 28 minutes on the front end of back-to-back games. Tyler Kolek scored 12 points and provided a spark in the second quarter as the backup to Brunson, Andre Drummond grabbed 14 rebounds in 15 minutes, and Deuce McBride had eight points and New York outscored Milwaukee by 39 while he was on the floor.

Jaime Jaquez Jr. scored 16 points and Ryan Rollins had 14 for the Bucks, who lost their seventh straight and fell to 1-10. They played without leading scorer Tyler Herro, who missed his first game of the season because of a bruised right knee.

PHOENIX (AP) — Jordan Goodwin scored 18 points in his return from a calf injury, Devin Booker added 17 and Phoenix cruised past Los Angeles.

Phoenix shot 22 of 43 (51%) from 3-point range and had seven players score in double digits, including five who came off the bench. Luke Kennard had 14 points, Jalen Green scored 13 and Collin Gillespie added 12 points and eight assists while Khaman Maluach contributed 11 points and seven rebounds.

The Suns had a 17-point halftime lead and pushed the advantage to 91-59 with four minutes left in the third quarter. They have a 3-2 record so far on their season-long, seven-game homestand.

Goodwin — who signed a $19 million, three-year deal to return to the Suns during the offseason — made 6 of 7 shots from beyond the arc in just 14 minutes. He missed the past three games.

The Clippers were coming off their first win in more than two weeks, but have now lost eight of their last nine games. Rui Hachimura, Baba Miller and Darius Garland all scored 13 points while Max Strus had 12.

#2722. INTERVIEW: Dortmund hero Owomoyela anticipates "intense" renewed Revierderby rivalry with Schalke 04

Borussia Dortmund icon Patrick Owomoyela senses the Revierderby with arch rivals FC Schalke 04 may take time to regain its overall importance. This, he feels, is largely due to the Gelsenkirchen side’s three-year absence from the Bundesliga and their waining dominance.

“It is [a big game], but it hasn’t been there for so long now that people [from Dortmund and Schalke] were urging for it. However, it’s still something that’s far away,” Owomoyela told Bulinews.com and others at a media round table event in Munich last week.

“Even when they [Schalke] were still in the Bundesliga [most recently], it was still important for the fans, but it wasn’t as important for the outcome of the season compared to playing against Bayern.

“In my time, it was [very important]. Firstly, we were both competing for the championship, so the derby was the biggest game. You could lose all the games but if you won those two [against Schalke] it was a perfect season [for fans].

“At least it felt that way, but now it has changed. Now Bayern is the biggest rival. The fans are happy that it [the Revierderby] is back, but it’s not shining as brightly as it did during my years as a player.

“I mean, when we come to within two weeks or a week out from the game, then I am sure my feelings will change,” the Hamburg native said with a smile, casting his thoughts forward to the clubs’ first meeting in early December.

When asked if he would like to see the Royal Blues return to a level akin to the era of the 2010s which saw regular European football, the 46-year-old welcomed the idea. He reckons it would give the Ruhrpott’s heavyweight clash some added spice.

“It would be fantastic if it wasn’t just [an important fixture] for the pure rivalry, but also an important game for the [outcome of the] season. That would add to the importance of it and that would be something [special].

“It will be a fantastic game, it will be intense and a hard-fought fight, I’m sure. But of course [Schalke becoming more successful] would add a special ingredient to this derby for sure,” he said ahead of the early December encounter.

#2720. John Spytek: First "real" call on Kirk Cousins came this morning

As NFL trades slip into hibernation until March, it’s important to remember something the next time players can be sent from one team to another.

Teams push plenty of BS to the media — and the media often passes it along without scrutiny.

Case in point: The internally inconsistent claim made by ESPN on Saturday, undoubtedly based on information straight from the Raiders.

“As of this weekend,” Adam Schefter of ESPN tweeted, “the Raiders had not received any trade inquiries regarding their starting quarterback Kirk Cousins, nor are they interested in dealing him, per league sources. They plan to keep sticking with him until they believe their No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza is ready.”

So the Raiders hadn’t received any trade inquiries, but they weren’t interested in the trade inquiries they hadn’t received? Right.

In a press conference with reporters on Tuesday, Raiders G.M. John Spytek addressed how it all came to be.

“I never made one call on Kirk Cousins,” Spytek said. “And I got a few phone calls. But one real one this morning.”

The “real one” ultimately entailed getting a third-round pick for Cousins. Which further highlights how silly it is for a team to claim — and for the media to share — the idea that “WE’RE NOT INTERESTED.”

Everyone is interested in a trade offer for all but a small handful of players in the entire league. Anything else is posturing. And, as is often the case when it comes to NFL reporting, the insiders allow themselves to become extensions of the team’s P.R. department in an effort to send a given message.

The Raiders weren’t interested, until they were. And it didn’t take all that much to make them interested in giving up their starting quarterback.

It was easier to make the decision because they were surely thinking about when to bench him for rookie Fernando Mendoza. And it surely was easier for Cousins to embrace the trade, given that he’s now in a position to keep playing for a team that has a chance to get to the postseason and to make some noise in January.

#2719. York Catholic boys cruise past Dock Mennonite in PIAA 1A first round

Joe Nattans will take his starting lineup against any team in the state.

The York Catholic coach has never doubted his players. Not when they played in the SCAC tournament final, not when they won their first District 3 title since 2011 and not Tuesday night against Dock Mennonite in the PIAA Class 1A first round.

"When you get to this point in the season, every team's good," Nattans said. "But I told them I'd put our 11 up against anybody. We're playing with confidence, but we're also playing with understanding that we have to have our best game every time."

The Fighting Irish delivered on that expectation from Nattans in a 5-1 win over Dock Mennonite on Tuesday night. Russell Young led with two goals, and Landon Baker had two assists to push the Fighting Irish to their first trip to the PIAA quarterfinals since 2019.

Week 12 SCAC Football Preview: Win or go home: Week 12's District 3 football previews for SCAC teams

SCAC Football All-Stars: SCAC football coaches reveal 2026 all-stars, postseason awards

It didn't take long for the Irish to establish themselves. Young took the ball himself and scored in the fourth minute of regulation. The Irish added two more goals before the Pioneers could respond, with Kobin Proudfoot and Gabe Iroabuchi both scoring on crosses from Jonathan Baker and Derek Noel. Three of York Catholic's five goals were all scored on crosses.

When York Catholic wasn't putting up goals, it was pressuring Dock Mennonite's defense. Following Young's goal, the Irish put up consecutive shots in the Pioneers' box before they were cleared out.

"There's a lot of confidence," Young said. "Dock's a great team; we just really distributed the ball well tonight. We always seem to find space behind their defense, and then we took our chances."

Dock Mennonite found offensive opportunities late in the first half. While it scored once on a breakaway by senior Cade Jackson, York Catholic goalie Brady Prendergast shut every other shot down. Prendergast ended the game with two saves, and he and the rest of York Catholic's defense shut out Dock Mennonite through the second half.

"Had a few slip-ups back there, some balls getting through farther than I wanted to, but I was fully confident today that we were going to get it back," Prendergast said. "If for whatever reason they got a cross up or a shot off, I had full confidence in myself that I was going to save it and get it back up there."

With the Pioneers shut down, the Irish built their lead. Young scored his second goal in the 57th minute off an assist from Landon Baker, and Joey Kury set the final score in stone with a final goal with over a minute left in regulation.

The Fighting Irish now move on to the PIAA quarterfinals against District 11 champion Moravian Academy, with the match slated for Saturday, Nov. 14.

#2717. Jaguars-Ravens averages 13.96 million on Prime Video

When it comes to interpreting press releases regarding the audiences for sporting events, there’s a rule of thumb.

The higher the number appears in the release, the better the company thinks the audience is. The lower the number appears in the release, the less impactful the figure is.

And if the number is really bad, there’s no release at all.

For the Week 9 Thursday night game between the Jaguars and Ravens— which was destined to have a non-stellar audience thanks to the Ravens being down to their third-string quarterback — Prime Video led with the fact that the eight-game season-to-date average has outperformed last year’s numbers.

The 33-10 win by the Jaguars, which Prime Video accurately called “lopsided” in the release, generated an average of 13.96 million viewers.

It nevertheless was, as Prime Video notes, a 13-percent bump over last year’s Week 9 Thursday night game. And for good reason. The Week 9 Thursday night game in 2025 featured the Ravens at the Dolphins, a 28-6 Baltimore win.

Even with an audience of less than 14 million in the eighth TNF game of the season, the package is offering 17.15 million per week for 2026.

This week’s game — Commanders at Giants — should do well, given that the Giants are both doing well and occupy the nation’s top market. In Week 11, it’s Colts at Texans. Which won’t be great.

The following week, Prime Video has a potentially massive game on Black Friday between the currently 7-2 Broncos and 6-2 Steelers.

After that, it’s Chiefs-Rams, Vikings-Patriots, 49ers-Chargers, Texans-Eagles (on Christmas Eve), and Ravens-Bengals.

#2715. Injury pileup gets bigger: Brandon Williams out at least a week

Last night, Brandon Williams lasted just 99 seconds before sustaining an injury that kept him out the rest of the game. This afternoon, following an MRI, we've learned that it's a mild left hamstring strain that will keep him out for at least a week, which will be when he's next evaluated by the Golden State Warriors medical staff. It's a big blow for both the fifth-year vet and the team as this next 5-game stretch, already figuring to be the end of this historic winning streak at some point, could be a real setback.

As Brady mentioned last night, Williams joins Jimmy Butler III, Moses Moody, and Gary Payton II among the actively injured with Will Richard out indefinitely and Kristaps Porziņģis all but retired. That's 10 points, 2 rebounds, and 2 assists in 16 minutes a night that they'll have to make up in the near-term. It's not like solid backup point guards are easy to find, and the Dubs are already without a true center on top of all these injured forwards.

Still, it's worth wondering to what extent the team expected this. He had a bout of quad tightness a little over a week ago and was ruled out against the Suns; and as Anthony Slater noted earlier:

But left hamstring issues have followed Williams early in his NBA career. He strained it in the 2025 preseason while with Dallas and subsequently missed time last March while dealing with tightness.

The Warriors will need him back ASAP, but it's also early enough in the season where there's probably some incentive to let him take extra time to recover. All that to say that 7 days is probably the most optimistic recovery period. They're one of the trickiest injuries to deal with and it's probably easier to envision a far longer recovery period, especially since he had to come out of the game so suddenly.

So, the backup PG situation (non-Podziemski division) looks like this: De'Anthony Melton, Gui Santos, and LJ Cryer. Williams was a perfect change of pace. Like a shot of espresso off the bench. He provided such a jolt that that alone might be the hardest aspect of his game to reproduce in the aggregate.

#2711. Jordan Poole would like to come home

The Golden State Warriors had a poignant reunion on Monday night, when they welcomed the New Orleans Pelicans to town, and proceeded to crush them by 51 points. There are a lot of former Warriors around the league, but some feel different when they face the Warriors, and that was the case when Jordan Poole checked into the game.

It's no secret that it's been a rough few years for Poole, whom the Warriors took with the 28th pick of the 2019 NBA Draft out of Michigan. After showing some signs in his first two seasons, Poole burst onto the scene during the 2021-22 campaign, when he became a starter, played 30 minutes a night, averaged 18.5 points and 4.0 assists, led the NBA in free throw percentage, had a highlight every game, and was at times the second option on a Warriors team that would eventually defeat the Boston Celtics to win an NBA championship.

But things went sideways for there. The next year was bittersweet, as Poole parlayed his performance into a massive extension, but was also on the receiving end of a punch from teammate Draymond Green, which led to uncomfortable vibes and thick tension for the entire year. The next offseason, the Warriors traded Poole to the Washington Wizards for Chris Paul, and, away from the confines of Steph Curry and Steve Kerr's offense, Poole struggled, putting up big numbers but on very low efficiency.

He bounced back with a strong offensive showing in 2024-25, but prior to last season was traded to the Pelicans. His first year in the bayou did not go according to plan, as he averaged just 13.4 points and shot a lowly 37.2% from the field.

This year has been even worse. Poole started the season slow, coming off the bench in the first four games of the season and having lackluster numbers. That earned him a benching, and when New Orleans came to town on Monday, Poole had gone six straight games without getting on the court.

That playing drought ended on Monday. With the Pelicans down a handful of key players — including Zion Williamson, Trey Murphy III, and Yves Missi — and with the game a blowout from the start, Jamahl Mosley gave Poole his largest run of the season, playing him for 34 minutes. Poole didn't play well — he scored seven points on 1-for-5 shooting, with two assists and two turnovers — but it was still nice seeing him out there. And it was hard not to wonder: what could have been?

Maybe we'll get something of an answer someday. While Poole has been reluctant to discuss the situation with Green, Monday was the first time that he really spoke about his time in Golden State. And he didn't hide his feelings: he misses it.

Asked by reporters if he missed Golden State, Poole made his thoughts emphatically clear, saying, "Hell yeah! Obviously. They play the right way, bro. They play good basketball. They play team basketball … Do I miss it? Hell yeah."

Poole then spoke very openly about the difficulties of the current season, where he's struggling to find minutes on a team that is likely headed for the lottery. He didn't make excuses or cast blame anywhere, but repeated twice that the season — only a few weeks old — has been "pretty f*****g difficult."

His answer led to an obvious follow-up: would Poole, who will be an unrestricted free agent after the season, be amenable to a return to the Bay Area? Again, he left no doubt with his response, saying, "Yes. Yes. It just feels like home though, you know? Driving into the f*****g arena, crossing the Bay Bridge or wherever you're coming from, it definitely feels natural. And I think it's pretty evident, the way that I play is very fitting to how I used to play here. Nothing's changed, other than the systems that I'm in. We won a championship, you know, so it works … so to answer your question: definitely."

Poole elaborated, all but saying that he would jump at the opportunity to sign with the Dubs in free agency, should he be offered a contract. "I'm a free agent at the end of this season," the 27-year old explained. "If there's any place where I'm comfortable, it's probably where I started. So I just got to find ways to keep learning and try to make the best decisions for my future."

Barring something unexpected, the Warriors should have no problems finding the money to sign Poole next offseason, since his current play has tanked his value. A reunion would likely come down to whether or not the team felt they had a need for his services, and whether they believed he could bounce back following a few down years. He certainly seems like the ideal change-of-scenery candidate, and the Warriors are very familiar with his game and his work habits. They're always on the lookout for bench scorers, and especially could end up needing him if Brandon Williams departs next summer.

That's a long ways from now. But who knows: maybe this time next year, Poole will be back in a Warriors jersey. It sure sounds like he'd like that.

#2710. Nick Sirianni denies giving subtle middle finger to fans
